title: moonbuggy perf-harness output document (D2 numbers pipe)
description: One machine-readable row of performance numbers produced by a moonbuggy benchmark harness run. Every field a consumer of perf numbers depends on is frozen here; a change that adds, renames, or re-types a key raises the schema version rather than silently shifting the contract. This document is the single source of truth for perf numbers -- numbers quoted in docs, dashboards, or PRs must come from a conforming document.

schema.description: Version of this contract. Every conforming document carries it so a reader with one line knows exactly what that line means.

suite.description: Which workload or suite was measured. One of the canonical shapes (fast-tests, slow-tests, many-files) or a fixture name.

hypothesis.description: The perf-hypotheses tag this measurement belongs to (e.g. H21), or the literal 'baseline' for an untagged reference run. A hypothesis tag is what lets a dashboard group the numbers that measure one idea.

harness.description: The script that emitted the row, e.g. bench_mutation.py.

commit.description: Git commit (short or full) the numbers were measured on. A perf number is a fact about a specific snapshot of code, so the snapshot is part of the contract.

timestamp.description: When the row was produced, UTC.

wall_clock.description: Reported run time in seconds -- the median over `runs` where a harness takes more than one measurement.

runs.description: How many runs the median in wall_clock is over. A single measurement is runs=1; the A/B and profile harnesses default higher.

mutants_per_sec.description: mutants / wall_clock. The throughput figure that makes raw wall-clock comparable between machines that run different mutant counts.

memory_delta.description: Signed peak-RSS difference in bytes between the candidate and its comparator (baseline ref, or the unprofiled run). Zero when a single measurement has no comparator.

memory_baseline_bytes.description: The peak-RSS bytes memory_delta is differenced against. Absent when there is no comparator.

median.description: Pass-through of the harness's per-run median wall clock, equal to wall_clock when wall_clock already is the median.

interval.description: The harness's 95% confidence interval on the median, when it produces one (the A/B harness does).
